summary: This note is an excerpt from a Wikipedia article on Minneapolis, describing its geography, water resources, economic history, and business standing. It notes the city sits on both banks of the Mississippi River next to Saint Paul, has many lakes and waterways, was once a flour milling and timber hub, and is a major business center with several Fortune 500 headquarters.
one_line: Overview of Minneapolis, Minnesota: its Mississippi River location, abundant lakes and parkways, milling history, and role as a major corporate center.
key_facts: Minneapolis lies on both banks of the Mississippi River, just north of the river's confluence with the Minnesota River.
Minneapolis adjoins Saint Paul, the state's capital.
Minneapolis has 13 lakes, along with wetlands, the Mississippi River, creeks and waterfalls.
Many of Minneapolis's lakes are connected by parkways in the Chain of Lakes and the Grand Rounds National Scenic Byway.
Minneapolis was once the world's flour milling capital.
Minneapolis was once a hub for timber.
The city and surrounding region is the primary business center between Chicago and Seattle.
As of 2018, Minneapolis was home to 6 Fortune 500 companies.
As of 2018, the Twin Cities were the fifth-largest hub of major corporate headquarters in the United States.
Minneapolis is categorized as a global city because it is an integral link to the global economy.
